text: El partido entre Harbour City y Seabrook Town terminó 2-4 con un gran dominio del equipo visitante, que tuvo más oportunidades claras de gol (xG 3.44, es decir, hicieron ocasiones para meter casi 3 o 4 goles, frente a 1.03 de Harbour) [#1104]. Después de quedarse con 10 jugadores por la expulsión de Joon Whitfield a los 43 minutos [#871], Harbour City comenzó ganando 2-0 con goles de Elias Okafor y Marek Barros, este último jugador fue el mejor del partido con un gol, 2 asistencias y 5 pases claves [#975]. Pero Seabrook Town cambió su estilo a presionar más y jugar directo a partir del minuto 65, lo que les permitió ganar fuerza y remontar el partido con 4 goles en la segunda mitad [#1361]. Kian Romano fue clave, anotando dos goles seguidos en los dos minutos adicionales, uno con una ocasión que suele marcarse 6 de cada 10 veces y otro con una jugada casi segura para un gol [#1882] [#1906].

Marek Barros brilló con gol y dos asistencias, pero no fue suficiente.
Kian Romano fue la estrella con dos goles decisivos en el descuento.

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in es

- Seabrook Town’s comeback and eventual win was shaped by a shift in their tactical approach at 65’, increasing pressing intensity, line height, and directness in play. This change aimed to regain control and create chances more rapidly after trailing 2-1, reflecting a flexible adaptation to the game state by coach Mara Lindholm [1361].
- The counterattack was a key pattern late in the match: Kian Romano’s goal at 90+2’ came directly from a quick regain and a through ball assist, enabling a fast break to level the score. This shows Seabrook’s ability to exploit spaces quickly, tied to their 3-4-3 formation which facilitates wide attacking and rapid transitions [1882].
- Harbour City’s goals emerged from patient, short-passing build-ups characteristic of their 4-2-3-1 formation and style. The build-up to Elias Okafor’s goal involved 17 passes over nearly a minute, emphasizing control and patient probing rather than rapid transitions or direct long balls [904-905].
- Harbour City’s second goal came from a set piece—a corner with only one pass in the build-up before a long cross to Marek Barros scoring from distance—illustrating their mix of patient possession with occasional direct exploitation of set-piece opportunities, though they were less effective under pressure later [973-975].

- Seabrook Town dominated with a higher xG of 3.44 vs Harbour City's 1.03, reflecting their stronger attacking threat throughout the match [#1104].
- Kian Romano scored two late goals at 90+2' and 90+3', with high xG values of 0.605 and 0.952, crucial for Seabrook Town's comeback and eventual win [#1882, #1906].
- Marek Barros, despite playing for the losing team, had the best rating (9.8) with 1 goal, 2 assists, and 5 key passes, showing his individual impact [#975].
- Harbour City received a red card for Joon Whitfield at 43', reducing them to 10 men before halftime and impacting their defensive stability [#871].
- Seabrook Town increased pressing and directness in play after 65', leading to 4 second-half goals and a momentum shift [#1361].
